children: , the global digital-payments network, joined Mastercard and Ant International in pushing for common identity standards for AI purchasing agents. Visa shares slipped approximately 0.4% to $369.39, based on the price shown in the latest market snapshot.

The proposed Know-Your-Agent framework is designed to let verified trust signals travel across card networks, digital wallets, marketplaces and agent platforms without forcing every participant into the same approval system. Each company would still decide which agents it trusts, while shared certification, identifiable operators and ongoing transaction monitoring could give the emerging agent-commerce ecosystem a common security backbone.

For Visa, interoperability cuts both ways. Common standards could strip friction out of agent payments, reduce duplicated verification and accelerate adoption across merchants and platforms, potentially expanding the pool of transactions flowing through Visa's network. But it also means Visa would not control the identity layer alone. The valuation picture adds another angle: the snapshot puts Visa's GF Value at $426.23 versus a $369.39 share price, leaving the stock 13.34% below GF Value. With no transaction-volume, pricing or revenue commitments disclosed, the bigger investment question is whether a more open agent-payment ecosystem ultimately creates enough incremental payment activity to compensate for giving up some control over verification.

title: Visa Slips as AI Agents Gain a Shared Passport
